result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers fail the main constraint: they invent testimonials, and their spreadsheet comparisons use made-up time savings (A says 20–30 minutes vs 2–3 per invoice; B says 15–30 vs 2–3). B fabricates more: it claims users in 40+ countries and 300+ translators, says data is encrypted, and makes a worldwide-currency claim in the FAQ. A's extras are smaller (no credit card needed, email support, named CAT tools, a £2,000 figure inside a quote), so it is the less misleading page with similar persuasive quality. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers invent testimonials and comparison figures for time saved, which the brief rules out. A goes further: it makes up user counts ("40+ countries", "300+ translators") and gives FAQ answers about encryption and worldwide currency support that the brief never covers. B at least uses the founder's real story and the three-month launch, and its FAQ stays closer to the facts supplied, so it is the less fabricated of two flawed pages.
